views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not add another increment of escalation on top of the already-scheduled List 4A tariffs. Keep the September Washington talks, leave the existing 25% on ~$250B and the Huawei Entity List in place as leverage, and treat the August 23 extra 5-point hike plus the “leave China” directive as bargaining chips rather than faits accomplis. Use the next round to test whether Beijing will restore farm purchases and re-engage on enforcement/IP text; do not offer unilateral rollback or purchase-side concessions without a matching, enforceable offer.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material, not existential. After the Osaka “no new tariffs for the time being” truce (2019-06-29) and a low-yield Shanghai round (2019-07-30), Washington announced List 4 on ~$300B (2019-08-01), Treasury labeled China a currency manipulator after CNY broke 7 (2019-08-05), and Beijing answered by suspending U.S. farm purchases and, on 2019-08-23, 5–10% tariffs on ~$75B including soy, crude, aircraft, plus a Dec 15 restart of 25% auto duties. USTR has already split List 4 so phones/laptops/toys wait until Dec 15 (2019-08-13), which is an implicit admission that consumer incidence is now the binding U.S. constraint. Markets are pricing that risk: the 10-year yield fell from 2.72% in early March to 1.47% on 2019-08-28; the 2s10s curve inverted again on Aug 23 and the 3m–10s inversion was the deepest since 2007. The Fed cut funds to 2.13% in August, and Powell at Jackson Hole said trade-policy uncertainty is already weakening U.S. manufacturing and capital spending and that monetary policy cannot write a “rulebook for international trade.” Farm Bureau called the ag halt a “body blow” after China’s U.S. farm imports fell from $19.5B (2017) to $9.1B (2018), despite ~$28B in aid. That is high-but-not-existential territory (~+0.4): key export sector hit, incoming consumer tariffs, recession signal — but Powell still described the expansion as close to the dual mandate. Further escalation (the extra 5pp, forced decoupling, more entity-list moves) would likely deepen the inversion, raise holiday-price risk, and give Beijing a pretext to skip September talks. Unilateral concession is also wrong: China walked back structural text in May, used the yuan and farm boycott as weapons, and still has not offered an enforcement mechanism. Negotiate without new commitments is the stance that preserves leverage while stopping the tit-for-tat from becoming the recession the bond market is already discounting.
key_factors: Osaka truce broken then List 4 / manipulator designation / $75B China retaliation in three weeks
U.S. farm sector already cut in half vs 2017 and now facing a purchase halt plus Dec 15 auto tariffs
List 4A consumer incidence and Dec 15 delay show the tariff tool is now hitting U.S. households
10-year at 1.47%, inverted curve, August Fed cut, Powell linking trade uncertainty to weak capex
September Washington round still scheduled — a live off-ramp that further escalation could close
Structural IP/tech-transfer/enforcement issues remain unresolved; Huawei Entity List is separate national-security leverage

sources_cited.excerpt: G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs "for the time being."
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
USTR splits List 4: List 4A effective Sept 1; List 4B (cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel) delayed to Dec 15.

China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods (5–10%, split Sept 1 / Dec 15), including re-imposing tariffs on US autos. Trump orders firms to look for an alternative to China and directs a 5-point increase on planned List 4.
U.S. 10-year Treasury yield 1.47% on 2019-08-28, down 1.25pp (~46%) from early March.
Federal funds effective rate 2.13% in August 2019, down from 2.40% in July (first easing step of the cycle).
China halted U.S. farm purchases; Farm Bureau called it a body blow. China farm imports from the U.S. fell from $19.5B in 2017 to $9.1B in 2018; up to $28B in U.S. farm aid.

Powell: trade policy uncertainty seems to be playing a role in the global slowdown and in weak manufacturing and capital spending in the United States; monetary policy cannot provide a settled rulebook for international trade.
China 5–10% tariffs on $75B in two batches matching U.S. dates; 25% on U.S. cars Dec 15; talks still slated for early September in Washington.
U.S. yield-curve inversion deepened to levels not seen since 2007; 10-year yields near 1.49% with 3m–10s as wide as 52bp.
